cvs: 'Asplenifolia' – fern-leaved but broader and more open · 'Columnaris' (Tallhedge) – narrow upright with normal oval leaves, used for hedging
foliage: deciduous; very narrow, wavy, thread-like dark green leaves turning yellow in autumn
hardinessNote: Very hardy throughout the UK, coping with winters colder than -20°C.
pollination: not applicable; grown for foliage and form, sets little fruit
prune: Little needed. Lightly trim in late winter to keep the column tight or remove any stray stems.
resilience: Very cold-hardy and tolerant of damp soils and urban conditions. Pests: largely trouble-free; occasional aphids.
toxicity: Berries and bark are poisonous if eaten, causing vomiting and diarrhoea. Keep away from children, dogs and cats. This form sets few berries.
uncertain: height: RHS 1.5–2.5 m; Nature Hills 1.5–2.1 m; Clarenbridge 2.5 m
seed: US sources say seed is mostly non-viable so it is not invasive like the species; not a UK concern since F. alnus is native
uses: Narrow screening · vertical accent in small or contemporary gardens · large containers · formal rows
visual: Narrow upright column of feathery thread-like leaves · butter-yellow autumn colour
water: Water regularly through the first year until roots establish, then only in long dry spells.
